metadata.title: Noncirrhotic Nonalcoholic Steatohepatitis With Liver Fibrosis: Developing Drugs for Treatment
metadata.topic: Draft guideline · FDA human drugs and biologics
metadata.legal_basis: FDA Guidance Document (21 CFR 10.115). Guidance states FDA's current thinking and is not binding unless a statute or regulation requires it; the official text governs.

metadata_verification: Source-register metadata; dates and legal status require human verification.

candidates.statement: In general, FDA’s guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable responsibilities. 27 Instead, guidances describe the Agency’s current thinking on a topic and should be viewed only 28 as recommendations, unless specific regulatory or statutory requirements are cited. The use of 29 the word should in Agency guidances means that something is suggested or recommended, but 30 not required. 31
candidates.context: This guidance does not address the clinical development of drugs for the treatment of cirrhosis 23 caused by NASH. This guidance also does not address the clinical development of in vitro 24 diagnostic (IVD) devices that may assist in drug development for NASH. 2 1 This guidance has been prepared by the Division of Gastroenterology and Inborn Error Products in the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research at the Food and Drug Administration.

candidates.statement: 2 This guidance does not address the regulatory issues related to commercial development of an IVD device to identify a specific biomarker, which may require FDA clearance or approval of the IVD. Manufacturers interested in pursuing the development of a specific assay for commercial use should consult the Office of In Vitro Diagnostics and Radiological Health in the Center for Devices and Radiological Health. For further information on the process for obtaining an investigational device exemption for an IVD, see the guidance for sponsors, clinical investigators, institutional review boards, and FDA staff FDA Decisions for Investigational Device Exemption Clinical Investigations . We update guidances periodically. To make sure you have the most recent version of a guidance, check the FDA guidance web page at https://www.fda.gov/RegulatoryInformation/Guidances/default.htm .

Patient inclusion criteria 201 • Patients should have a histological diagnosis of NASH with liver fibrosis made close to 206 the time of trial enrollment (i.e., no more than 6 months before enrollment). Pediatric Considerations 367

candidates.statement: Pediatric NASH appears to have different histological characteristics as well as a different 369 natural history when compared to adult NASH. For reasons that are currently unknown, disease 370 characteristics and progression in pediatric patients may be different. In addition, the common 371 histologic findings of ballooning degeneration, classic zone-3 fibrosis, and parenchymal 372 inflammation observed in adult NASH are less common in children with NASH. Therefore, 373 applying the adult scoring system to children with NASH may be challenging. Sponsors of 374 drugs for the treatment of noncirrhotic NASH with liver fibrosis should consider the following 375 for pediatric studies: 376
candidates.context: D. Pediatric Considerations 367 • Given all the differences mentioned, extrapolation of efficacy from adults to pediatric 378 patients solely on pharmacokinetic or pharmacodynamic information is not appropriate at 379 this time. However, gathering robust exposure-response information during adult trials 380 can be critical to inform the ability to extrapolate in the future. 381

candidates.statement: • The risk/benefit of each drug will determine the overall timing of the pediatric studies in 387 relation to the adult clinical trials. Sponsors should consider initiating pediatric studies 388 once sufficient information about dosing, safety, and efficacy in adults is obtained. 389
candidates.context: • Longitudinal natural history data in pediatric patients are needed to better characterize the 383 disease course, identify inclusion/exclusion criteria for future clinical studies, and support 384 choice of endpoints for pediatric studies. 385 • Pediatric studies in noncirrhotic NASH pose additional challenges.
